name: Mirror checking / mirror avoidance

lead: Mirror checking means repeatedly inspecting one's appearance; mirror avoidance means steering clear of mirrors. Both are described in body dysmorphic disorder.
Sources specific to how these habits appear in looksmaxxing culture are thin.

paras: In BDD they are treated as rituals that maintain preoccupation; CBT with exposure and response prevention targets them.
They are described as time-consuming and linked to distress in BDD; clinicians evaluate them as part of diagnosis.

lead: Mirror checking and mirror avoidance are two opposite behavioral patterns around reflective surfaces that are described in body dysmorphic disorder (BDD). Wikipedia lists repetitive checking of one's appearance as a characteristic behavior of BDD and notes that some people instead avoid mirrors.[1]

In looksmaxxing communities the terms describe self-monitoring habits tied to appearance anxiety. Research on them is mainly within the BDD literature, where exposure and response prevention targets such rituals.
infobox: Exposure and response prevention within CBT

paras: Wikipedia describes mirror checking as one of several repetitive behaviors in BDD, alongside reassurance seeking, comparing with others, camouflaging with clothing or cosmetics, excessive grooming and skin picking.[1] The same article says some people with BDD avoid mirrors instead.[1]
People with BDD may spend several hours a day or more preoccupied with the perceived flaw.[1]

No studies found specific to mirror checking or avoidance in looksmaxxing communities. Cognitive-behavioral treatment for BDD, which includes exposure with response prevention aimed at rituals such as checking, has been studied in randomized trials more broadly; see CBT for BDD.
